taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit: a shrub (FEIS, Howard 1993).

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's devilsclub review (Howard 1993, read 2026-10-15): "an erect to slightly spreading, deciduous shrub from 3.3 to 10 feet (1-3 m) in height".

traits.fruit_type.note: FEIS's devilsclub review (Howard 1993, read 2026-10-15): "The fruit is a drupe with two to three seeds".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as no source read gives it.

traits.fruit_size_m.note: Wikipedia, Oplopanax horridus (read 2026-10-19, citing Pojar and MacKinnon, Plants of the Pacific Northwest Coast): the fruit a small red drupe 4-7 mm across.

traits.flowering_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence high), as the FEIS review read gives no months.

generator.params.note: Red-flowering currant's values, changed by hand for devil's club (its few, thick stems with their leaves at the top, their branching and their lean now come from the Oplopanax rules and its stated stem clump, Rosaceae review round 2, 2026-10-19): few, thick, upright, sparsely branched stems (FEIS, Howard 1993: "sparsely branched with sharp, dense prickles on stems") with dense prickles, and huge palmate leaves held flat near the stem tips over a terminal panicle of red fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 1.8 m at 12 years in the open, within FEIS's 1-3 m (Howard 1993). Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye: large, shallowly 7-lobed, sharply toothed leaves on long stalks; pale tan prickly stems. Its flowers and fruit (appearance.organs.bloom) are drawn by the rules at the flowering plants from its stated characters (Rosaceae review, 2026-10-19); the hand-set cluster had drawn each fruit about 4 cm across against the 4-7 mm drupes its sources give.

traits.height_typical_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L141937), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_width_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L141937), as no source read gives it.

traits.leaf_margin.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L141937), as no source read gives it.

traits.sexual_system.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L141937), as no source read gives it.

traits.inflorescence_length_m.note: A model estimate (confidence high, record L141937), as no source read gives it.

traits.flower_colour.note: Wikipedia, Oplopanax horridus (read 2026-10-19, citing Pojar and MacKinnon, Plants of the Pacific Northwest Coast): each flower small, with five greenish-white petals; sRGB by eye for the words.

traits.fruit_colour_ripe.note: Wikipedia, Oplopanax horridus (read 2026-10-19, citing Pojar and MacKinnon, Plants of the Pacific Northwest Coast): a small red drupe; sRGB by eye for the word.

traits.flower_size_m.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: flowers 4-7 mm across: small, five-petalled (Wikipedia), up to 7 mm long (Lake Country Museum's wildflower page, read 2026-10-19).

traits.units_per_inflorescence.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: 100-300 flowers: dense umbels gathered in a panicle 10-20 cm across (Wikipedia), each umbel of some ten to twenty flowers.

traits.inflorescence_branches.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: 8-20 branches, each ending in its umbels, in a pyramidal panicle as photographs show it.

traits.stem_clump.note: FEIS's devilsclub review (Howard 1993, read 2026-10-19): sparsely branched; it reproduces vegetatively by rhizomes and/or layering and may sprout from the root crown, so a plant stands on a few stems from its base.
